paragraphs.sourceText: How a Poor, Abandoned Parisian Boy Became a Top Chef
paragraphs.translationZh: 一个贫穷、被遗弃的巴黎男孩如何成为顶级厨师

paragraphs.sourceText: A. The busy streets in Paris were uneven and caked in thick mud, but there was always a breathtaking sight to see in the shop windows of Patisserie de la Rue de la Paix. By 1814, people crowded outside the bakery, straining for a glimpse of the latest sweet food created by the young chef who worked inside.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：巴黎繁忙的街道凹凸不平，积满了厚厚的泥土，但和平街糕点店的橱窗里总能看到令人惊叹的景象。到了 1814 年，人们挤满了面包店外面，争先恐后地想一睹里面工作的年轻厨师创造的最新甜品。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. His name was Marie-Antoine Carême, and he had appeared, one day, almost out of nowhere. But in his short lifetime, which ended exactly 184 years ago today, he would forever revolutionize French gourmet food （美食）, write best-selling cook books and think up magical dishes for royals and other important people.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 他的名字叫玛丽·安托万·卡莱姆，有一天，他几乎凭空出现。但在他短暂的一生中，也就是 184 年前的今天，他永远彻底改变了法国美食，撰写了畅销烹饪书籍，并为皇室成员和其他重要人物发明了神奇的菜肴。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. Carême's childhood was one part tragedy, equal part mystery. Born the 16th child to poor parents in Paris in either 1783 or 1784, a young Carême was suddenly abandoned at the height of the French Revolution. At 8 years old, he worked as a kitchen boy for a restaurant in Paris in exchange for room and board. By age 15, he had become an apprentice （学徒） to Sylvain Bailly, a well-known dessert chef with a successful bakery in one of Paris's most fashionable neighborhoods.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. Carême 的童年一半是悲剧，一半是神秘。年轻的卡雷姆于 1783 年或 1784 年出生于巴黎，是贫困家庭的第 16 个孩子，在法国大革命最激烈的时期突然被遗弃。 8岁时，他在巴黎一家餐厅当厨房男孩，以换取食宿。 15 岁时，他成为著名甜点师西尔万·贝利 (Sylvain Bailly) 的学徒，后者在巴黎最时尚的街区之一拥有一家成功的面包店。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Carême was quick at learning in the kitchen. Bailly encouraged his young apprentice to learn to read and write. Carême would often spend his free afternoons at the nearby National Library reading books on art and architecture. In the back room of the little bakery, his interest in design and his baking talent combined to work wonders—he shaped delicious masterpieces out of flour, butter and sugar.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. Carême 在厨房里学得很快。贝利鼓励他年轻的学徒学习读书和写作。卡雷姆经常在附近的国家图书馆度过空闲的下午，阅读有关艺术和建筑的书籍。在小面包店的后屋里，他对设计的兴趣和烘焙天赋结合在一起创造了奇迹——他用面粉、黄油和糖塑造了美味的杰作。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. In his teenage years, Carême fashioned eatable copies of the late 18th century's most famous buildings—cookies in the shape of ruins of ancient Athens and pies in the shape of ancient Chinese palaces and temples. Sylvain Bailly, his master, displayed these luxuriant creations—often as large as 4 feet tall—in his bakery windows.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 在他十几岁的时候，Carême 制作了 18 世纪末最著名的建筑的可食用复制品——古雅典遗址形状的饼干和中国古代宫殿和寺庙形状的馅饼。他的师傅西尔万·贝利 (Sylvain Bailly) 在他的面包店橱窗里展示了这些华丽的作品，通常高达 4 英尺。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. Carême's creations soon captured the discriminating eye of a French diplomat, Charles Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord. Around 1804, Talleyrand challenged Carême to produce a full menu for his personal castle, instructing the young baker to use local, seasonal fruits and vegetables and to avoid repeating main dishes over the course of an entire year. The experiment was a grand success and Talleyrand's association with French nobility would prove a profitable connection for Carême.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. Carême 的创作很快就引起了法国外交官 Charles Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord 挑剔的目光。 1804 年左右，塔列朗要求卡雷姆为他的私人城堡制作一份完整的菜单，指导这位年轻的面包师使用当地的时令水果和蔬菜，并避免全年重复主菜。这次实验取得了巨大成功，塔列朗与法国贵族的联系将为 Carême 带来有利可图的联系。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. French Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte was known to be unimpressed by the declining taste of early 18th century cooking, but under pressure to entertain Paris's high society, he too called Carême to his kitchen at Tuileries Palace. In 1810, Carême designed the extraordinary cake for the wedding of Napoleon and his second bride, Marie-Louise of Austria. He became one of the first modern chefs to focus on the appearance of his table, not just the flavor of his dishes. “I want order and taste. A well-displayed meal is enhanced one hundred percent in my eyes,” he later wrote in one of his cook books.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 众所周知，法国皇帝拿破仑·波拿巴对 18 世纪初烹饪品味的下降并不以为然，但迫于招待巴黎上流社会的压力，他也将卡雷姆叫到了杜乐丽宫的厨房。 1810 年，Carême 为拿破仑和他的第二任新娘奥地利的玛丽·路易丝的婚礼设计了这款非凡的蛋糕。他成为第一批注重餐桌外观而不仅仅是菜肴风味的现代厨师之一。 “我想要秩序和味道。在我看来，一顿精心摆设的饭菜百分百美味，”他后来在一本烹饪书中写道。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. In 1816, Carême began a culinary (烹饪的) journey which would forever mark his place as history's first top chef. He voyaged to England to cook in the modern Great Kitchen of the prince regent (摄政王)，George Ⅳ, and crossed continents to prepare grand banquets for the tables of Tsar Alexander Ⅰof Russia. Never afraid to talk up his own accomplishments, a boastful Carême made a fortune as wealthy families with social ambitions invited him to their kitchens. Later, in his cook books, he would often include a sketch of himself, so that people on the street would be able to recognize—and admire—him.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 1816 年，Carême 开始了烹饪之旅，这将永远标志着他作为历史上第一位顶级厨师的地位。他远渡英国，在摄政王乔治四世的现代大厨房里做饭，并跨越大陆为俄罗斯沙皇亚历山大一世的餐桌准备盛大的宴会。自夸的卡雷姆从不害怕谈论自己的成就，当有社会抱负的富裕家庭邀请他到他们的厨房时，他发了大财。后来，在他的烹饪书中，他经常会附上自己的素描，以便街上的人们能够认出并钦佩他。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Carême's cooking displays became the symbol of fine French dining; they were plentiful, beautiful and imposing. Guests would fall silent in wonder as servants carried Carême's fancy creations into the dining hall. For a banquet celebrating the Grand Duke Nicholas of Russia's visit to George Ⅳ's Brighton Pavillion on Jan. 18, 1817, the menu featured 120 different dishes, highlighting eight different soups, 40 main courses, and 32 desserts.
paragraphs.translationZh: I. Carême 的烹饪展示成为法国高级餐饮的象征；它们数量众多、美丽而雄伟。当仆人将 Carême 的精美作品搬进餐厅时，客人们会惊讶地安静下来。 1817 年 1 月 18 日，庆祝俄罗斯大公尼古拉斯访问乔治四世布莱顿馆的宴会，菜单上有 120 种不同的菜肴，其中包括 8 种不同的汤、40 种主菜和 32 种甜点。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. As he traveled through the homes of early 19th century nobility, Carême forged the new art of French gourmet food. Locked in hot kitchens, Carême created his four “mother sauces.” These sauces—béchamel, velouté, espagnole and allemande—formed the central building blocks for many French main courses. He also perfected the soufflé—a baked egg dish, and introduced the standard chef's uniform—the same double-breasted white coat and tall white hat still worn by many chefs today. The white clothing conveyed an image of cleanliness, according to Carême—and in his realm, appearance was everything.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. Carême 在游历 19 世纪初贵族家庭的过程中，开创了法国美食的新艺术。卡雷姆被关在炎热的厨房里，创造了他的四种“母酱”。这些酱汁——白酱、丝绒酱、西班牙酱和阿勒曼德酱——构成了许多法国主菜的核心组成部分。他还完善了舒芙蕾——一种烤鸡蛋菜肴，并推出了标准厨师制服——如今许多厨师仍然穿着同样的双排扣白大衣和高高的白帽子。根据卡雷姆的说法，白色的衣服传达了一种干净的形象——在他的领域，外表就是一切。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Between meals, Carême wrote cook books that would be used in European kitchens for the next century. His manuals including The Royal Parisian Baker and the massive five-volume Art of French Cooking Series (1833-1847, completed after his death) first systematized many basic principles of cooking, complete with drawings and step-by-step directions. Long before television cooking shows, Carême walked readers through common kitchen tasks, instructing them to “try this for yourself, at home” as famous American Chef Julia Child might do, many years later.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 在两餐之间，卡雷姆写了一些烹饪书籍，这些书籍将在下个世纪的欧洲厨房中使用。他的手册包括《皇家巴黎面包师》和五卷本的《法国烹饪艺术系列》（1833-1847 年，在他去世后完成），首先系统化了许多烹饪的基本原理，并配有附图和分步说明。早在电视烹饪节目出现之前，Carême 就向读者介绍了常见的厨房任务，指导他们“自己在家尝试一下”，就像美国著名厨师朱莉娅·柴尔德（Julia Child）多年后可能会做的那样。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. In the end, however，it was the kitchen that did Carême in. Decades of working over coal fires in tight, closed spaces with little fresh air (to ensure his dishes would not get cold) had fatally damaged his lungs. On Jan. 12, 1833, Carême died just before he turned 50.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 然而，最终，卡雷姆还是被厨房害死了。几十年来，他一直在狭小、封闭的空间里，在几乎没有新鲜空气的情况下，在煤火上工作（以确保他的菜肴不会变冷），这对他的肺部造成了致命的损害。 1833 年 1 月 12 日，卡雷姆在 50 岁之前去世。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. But in his lifetime, Carême, ever confident, could see beyond his short domination in the kitchen. He wanted to “set the standard for beauty in classical and modern cooking, and prove to the distant future that the French chefs of the 19th century were the most famous in the world,” as he wrote in his papers.
paragraphs.translationZh: M：但在他的一生中，始终充满自信的卡雷姆能够超越他在厨房的短暂统治。正如他在论文中所写，他希望“为古典和现代烹饪的美感树立标准，并向遥远的未来证明 19 世纪的法国厨师是世界上最著名的”。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Decades later, chef Auguste Escoffier would build upon Carême's concept of French cuisine （烹饪）. But in the very beginning, there was just Carême, the top chef who elevated dining into art.
paragraphs.translationZh: 几十年后，主厨奥古斯特·埃斯科菲 (Auguste Escoffier) 以 Carême 的法式烹饪理念为基础。但一开始，只有Carême，这位将餐饮提升为艺术的顶级厨师。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Carême was among the first chefs who stressed both the appearance and flavor of dishes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. Carême 是最早注重菜肴外观和风味的厨师之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Carême wanted to show to later generations that French chefs of his time were most outstanding in the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. Carême 想向后人表明，他那个时代的法国厨师是世界上最杰出的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Carême benefited greatly from serving a French diplomat and his connections.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. Carême 因为法国外交官及其关系网服务而受益匪浅。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Carême learned his trade from a famous dessert chef in Paris.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. Carême 向巴黎一位著名的甜点师学习了他的手艺。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Carême's creative works were exhibited in the shop windows by his master.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. Carême 的创意作品被他的主人陈列在商店橱窗里。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Carême's knowledge of art and architecture helped him create extraordinary desserts out of ordinary ingredients.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. Carême 的艺术和建筑知识帮助他用普通原料制作出非凡的甜点。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Many people in Paris were eager to have a look at the latest sweet food made by Carême.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 许多巴黎人都迫不及待地想看看Carême最新推出的甜食。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Carême became extremely wealthy by cooking for rich and socially ambitious families.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. Carême 通过为富裕且有社会雄心的家庭做饭而变得极其富有。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Carême's writings dealt with fundamental cooking principles in a systematic way.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. Carême 的著作系统地讨论了基本的烹饪原则。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Carême's contribution to French cooking was revolutionary.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. Carême 对法国烹饪的贡献是革命性的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 and 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 46 和 50 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Roughly the size of a soda can, sitting on a bookshelf, a relatively harmless gadget may be turning friends away from your home. The elephant in your living room is your Internet-connected security camera, a device people are increasingly using for peace of mind in their homes. But few stop to think about the effect these devices may have on house guests. Should you tell your friends, for instance, that they're being recorded while you all watch the big game together?
paragraphs.translationZh: 一个大约有汽水罐那么大，放在书架上的相对无害的小玩意，可能会让你的朋友远离你的家。客厅里的大象是连接互联网的安全摄像头，人们越来越多地使用这种设备来让自己在家安心无忧。但很少有人停下来思考这些设备可能对客人产生的影响。例如，您是否应该告诉您的朋友，当你们一起观看大型比赛时他们正在被录制？

paragraphs.sourceText: “It's certainly new territory, especially as home security cameras become easier to install,” says Lizzie Post, president of the Emily Post Institute, America's foremost manners advisors. “I think it will be very interesting to see what etiquette （礼仪）emerges in terms of whether you tell people you have a camera or not, and whether guests have a right to ask that it be turned off, if it's not a security issue.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “这无疑是一个新领域，特别是当家庭安全摄像头变得更容易安装时，”美国最重要的礼仪顾问艾米丽·波斯特研究所所长利齐·波斯特说。 “我认为，如果不是安全问题，看看你是否告诉别人你有摄像头，以及客人是否有权要求关闭摄像头等礼仪，将会非常有趣。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Post wants to make clear that she's not talking about legal rights, but rather personal preferenc. She also wants to explain that there are no right or wrong answers regarding manners on this front yet, because the technology is just now becoming mainstream. Besides, the Emily Post Institute doesn't dictate manners.
paragraphs.translationZh: 波斯特想要澄清的是，她谈论的不是合法权利，而是个人偏好。她还想解释一下，关于这方面的礼仪，目前还没有正确或错误的答案，因为这项技术刚刚成为主流。此外，艾米莉·波斯特学院并不规定礼仪。

paragraphs.sourceText: When it comes to security cameras, Post says it's a host's responsibility to make sure guests feel comfortable within their home. “I'm always a fan of being open and honest.” For instance, if the host casually acknowledges that there is a camera in the room by telling a story about it, that may be enough to provide an opening for a guest to say if they are uncomfortable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 谈到安全摄像头，波斯特表示，房东有责任确保客人在家中感到舒适。 “我始终主张开放和诚实。”例如，如果主人通过讲述一个故事来随意承认房间里有一个摄像头，这可能足以为客人提供一个表达他们是否感到不舒服的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, if a contractor is working in your home, you don't need to tell them that there are cameras watching. Then again, the air of accountability that the camera generates can also work in contractors' favor. “If anything does go wrong while they're in the house, they don't want to be blamed for it,” she says. “In fact, the camera could be the thing that proves that they didn't steal the $20, or knock the vase off the table.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 但是，如果承包商在您家中工作，您无需告诉他们有摄像头在监视。话又说回来，摄像机产生的责任感也对承包商有利。 “如果他们在家里出现任何问题，他们不想因此受到指责，”她说。 “事实上，相机可以证明他们没有偷那 20 美元，也没有把花瓶从桌子上撞下来。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: PepsiCo is to spend billions of dollars to develop drinks and snacks and reformulate existing ones with lower sugar, salt and fat, as consumers demand healthier options and regulatory pressure intensifies amid an obesity epidemic （流行病）.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着消费者要求更健康的选择以及肥胖流行病带来的监管压力加剧，百事公司将斥资数十亿美元开发饮料和零食，并重新调整现有饮料和零食的糖、盐和脂肪含量。

paragraphs.sourceText: The maker of Mountain Dew and Gatorade has been one of the earlier movers in the industry to offer products with reduced levels of unhealthy ingredients—PepsiCo claims a packet of its chips now contains less salt than a slice of white bread. However, its new 10-year plan makes clear it believes it still has a long way to go.
paragraphs.translationZh: 激浪和佳得乐的制造商是业内较早推出减少不健康成分含量的产品的公司之一——百事公司声称，现在一包其薯片的含盐量比一片白面包还要少。然而，其新的十年计划明确表明，它相信还有很长的路要走。

paragraphs.sourceText: Shifting eating habits, including a sharp drop in consumption of sparkling drinks, have forced radical change on the industry. But those shifts have yet to be reflected in record obesity levels, which stand at 36.5% overall in the US.
paragraphs.translationZh: 饮食习惯的改变，包括气泡饮料消费量的急剧下降，迫使该行业发生根本性的变化。但这些变化尚未反映在创纪录的肥胖水平上，美国总体肥胖率为 36.5%。

paragraphs.sourceText: Indra Nooyi, PepsiCo chairman, said the plan to make its products healthier was important for the company's growth. But on the subject of obesity, she pointed out that consumers’ lifestyles have changed significantly, with many people being more sedentary （久坐不动的）not least because more time is spent in front of computers. She said PepsiCo's contribution was to produce healthier snacks that still tasted good.
paragraphs.translationZh: 百事可乐董事长英德拉·努伊 (Indra Nooyi) 表示，让产品更健康的计划对于公司的发展非常重要。但在肥胖问题上，她指出，消费者的生活方式已经发生了显着变化，许多人更加久坐不动，尤其是因为在电脑前花费了更多的时间。她说，百事可乐的贡献是生产出味道仍然不错的健康零食。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Society has to change its habits,” she added. “We can't do much to alter sedentary lifestyles, but we can provide consumers with great-tasting products, low in salt, sugar and fat. In the past we had to have a taste trade-off. But we're breaking that trade-off.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “社会必须改变习惯，”她补充道。 “我们无法做太多改变久坐的生活方式，但我们可以为消费者提供低盐、低糖、低脂肪的美味产品。过去我们必须在口味上进行权衡。但我们正在打破这种权衡。”

paragraphs.sourceText: PepsiCo's plan for its foods and drinks is based on guidelines from the World Health Organisation, which last week backed using taxes on sparkling drinks to reduce sugar consumption. Initiatives also include efforts to reduce its environmental impact, water consumption and materials used in packaging by 2025.
paragraphs.translationZh: 百事公司的食品和饮料计划是基于世界卫生组织的指导方针，该组织上周支持对气泡饮料征税以减少糖的消耗。举措还包括到 2025 年努力减少环境影响、水消耗和包装材料使用。

paragraphs.sourceText: PepsiCo did not say exactly how much it planned to invest to reach its goals. However, Dr Mehmood Khan, chief scientific officer, said the company had doubled research and development spending in the past five years and was “committed to sustaining investment”, adding that companies cannot cost-cut their way to increasing sales. PepsiCo's research and development budget in 2015 was $754 million.
paragraphs.translationZh: 百事公司没有具体透露计划投资多少来实现其目标。然而，首席科学官穆罕默德·汗博士表示，该公司在过去五年中研发支出增加了一倍，并“致力于维持投资”，并补充说，公司不能通过削减成本来增加销量。百事公司2015年的研发预算为7.54亿美元。
